svg.title: The CIA triad and the three conflicts its design means create
svg.desc: Confidentiality is delivered by encryption and segmentation, integrity by signatures, change control and immutable logs, availability by redundancy and capacity margin. Each means takes something away from the other two goals: encryption blinds inspection, traffic scrubbing hands visibility to a third party, and strict change control blocks the emergency edit that restores service fastest. A security design that does not say which goal was traded for which cannot be reviewed.
svg.text: CIA is a triangle of trade-offs, not three checkboxes
Every means that buys one goal takes something away from the other two — the design must say what was traded
C
Confidentiality
I
Integrity
A
Availability
seen only
by the entitled
usable when
it is needed
changed only by the entitled, and complete
the means: encryption in transit and at rest, access control, segmentation
hashing and signatures, change control, immutable logs
redundancy, capacity margin, DDoS mitigation, backup and recovery
1 · encryption against detection
Confidentiality encrypts the traffic; the IPS and the DLP then see nothing worth inspecting.
Terminate encryption at the inspection point, or accept that the segment is unobservable and
compensate with endpoint EDR and behaviour baselines — and write down which you chose.
2 · availability against confidentiality
Steering all traffic to a scrubbing centre to survive a DDoS hands it to a third party's eyes.
The mitigation is real; so is the exposure. Pick it per service, not per company, and scope
the contract to say what the provider may see and keep.
3 · integrity against availability
Strict baselines refuse the change made at 2 a.m. to restore service, and that change is often
the fastest path back. Allow the emergency path, then force the write-back: without the
second half, integrity becomes the reason the baseline is permanently wrong.
A security design that does not name the trades it made cannot be reviewed, and cannot be defended to an auditor or to the business when the bill arrives.
